test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If A's salary is 12% more than that of B, then by what percentage is B's salary less than that of A (correct to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct percentage reduction formula: **[r / (100 + r)] × 100**

Here, r = 12%

Reduction = [12 / (100 + 12)] × 100

Reduction = [12 / 112] × 100 ≈ 10.71%

**∴ The correct answer is 10.71%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A’s salary is 12% more than B’s salary.

**Formula Used:** Percentage Less = (Difference / Higher Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31d409ac551a02eab2470cacaed017af82f1d753748a0bdce07a013c84a7cf93.png] 

⇒ Let **B’s salary** = 100

⇒ **A’s salary** = 100 + 12% of 100 = 112

⇒ **Difference** = 112 − 100 = 12

⇒ **Percentage by which B is less than A** = (12 / 112) × 100

⇒ 3/28 × 100 = 300 / 28 = 75 / 7

⇒ 10.7142...

**∴ The correct answer is 10.71%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase/Decrease

If A is R% more than B, then B is [R / (100 + R)] × 100% less than A.

Inverse Case

If A is R% less than B, then B is [R / (100 − R)] × 100% more than A.

Fraction Equivalents

12% = 3/25. If B is 25, A is 25+3=28. B is 3/28 less than A. 1/28 ≈ 3.57%, so 3/28 ≈ 10.71%.</p
